title: Gradual traffic shift checklist and postmortem notes
content:
Quick context:
- Goal: validate v3.1.0 quantized runtime improvements on production workload for 48h without degrading tail latency or increasing cost beyond 3%.
- Method: progressive traffic shift from stable (v3.0) -> v3.1.0 via micro-batches + KV cache warming + pin fallback.
- Owner: Aisha Khan (primary), Liam Chen (metrics), Ruth Alvarez (rollback lead).

Pre-rollout checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
- [ ] Smoke tests on staging passed (latency, correctness) — PR #2421 green.
- [ ] Canary image baked and pushed to registry with consistent tags (redwood/runtime:v3.1.0-canary).
- [ ] Pinning policy reviewed and approved in release-config (pin-duration=15m, fallback-model=v3.0).
- [ ] Circuit-breaker thresholds configured: error-rate 0.5%, p99 latency +30% above baseline triggers immediate halt.
- [ ] Observability hooks in place: per-route latency, token-cost, user-facing error-rate, mem/gpu-util, prefix-hit ratio.
- [ ] Alerting runbook updated with playbook snippets (see linked Confluence page).
- [ ] Canary quota reserved in Dedicated pool (10% capacity) to avoid noisy neighbor.

Traffic shift plan (timeline, micro-batches):
- T0: baseline metrics capture (30m) — capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost/token, prefix cache-hit.
- T0+30m: release canary (1% traffic) for 15m. Monitor: real-time dashboard, slack alert channel #rollouts.
- T1: if stable, increase to 5% for 30m.
- T2: 15% for 1h after verifying tail latencies stable.
- T3: 30% for 2h.
- T4: 60% for 4h (longer to exercise batching regimes).
- T5: 100% if all checks pass (decision meeting required).

Stopping and rollback criteria (explicit):
- Any step: if error-rate > 0.5% absolute or +100% relative to baseline, stop and roll back to pinned variant.
- p99 latency increase > 20% sustained for 5m -> pause increase and investigate.
- Cost/unit increase > 3% sustained for 30m -> pause and investigate (cost signal owned by Liam).
- Unexpected fallback rates (client-observed errors) > 0.2% -> halt immediately.

Immediate rollback procedure (playbook):
1) Execute route policy: pin new requests to stable v3.0 (automated script: tools/rollout/pin-to-stable.sh --env=prod --reason=\"auto-rollback\").
2) Shrink canary pool to 0% and mark canary instances for graceful drain.
3) Notify #rollouts channel and escalate to SRE if infra hints (GPU OOMs, driver issues).
4) Open incident ticket INF-4562 if not already created; add timeline + logs.
5) Collect trace spans + sample requests for RCA.

Observability checklist (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route, tail for long-context requests.
- Errors: 4xx vs 5xx breakdown, model-level errors (generation truncated, decode errors).
- Resource: GPU util, free memory, OOMs, kernel restarts.
- Cache: prefix/KV cache hit ratio, cold-start counts.
- Cost: tokens-per-request and effective cost-per-sample (Liam metric).
- Signal integrity: ensure sampling of traces includes both stable and canary for apples-to-apples.

Data collection snippets (notes to self):
- Recommended KQL for p99 by route: logs | where service==\"runtime\" and model==\"v3.1.0-canary\" | summarize p99(latency_ms) by route
- Quick compare dashboard: baseline vs canary overlays, 30m rolling window.
- Dump sample requests with seeds for QA repro: tools/observability/sample-dump --model v3.1.0-canary --size 200

Postmortem notes (fill after run):
- Date of run: 2025-10-14 10:00 -> 2025-10-14 22:00 (10h active window).
- Outcome: reached 30% for 2h then auto-paused due to p99 spike on long-context route /chat/assistant.
- Timeline: 10:00 start (1%), 10:20 -> 5%, 11:00 -> 15%, 12:30 -> 30% (stable for 90m), 14:00 -> p99 spike detected +28% sustained -> pause.
- Root cause hypothesis: quantization kernel path under long-context sequences (seq>2048) produced slower attention kernel selection leading to increased compute time; combined with insufficient KV cache warmup for certain prefixes.
- Evidence collected: trace spans show increased token-generation time at layer attention-call for model v3.1.0-canary only, no infra OOM. Cache-hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 67% for affected prefixes.
- Immediate remediation attempted: extended KV warmup (prewarm script) improved cache-hit to 85% and reduced p99 by ~12% but not back to baseline.
- Final decision: roll back to v3.0 and open follow-ups for quant kernel fallback and more aggressive prewarm logic.

Action items / follow-ups (owners):
- [ ] SRE/Runtime: add fallthrough to legacy kernel for seq>2048 until quant path stable (Devon Park).
- [ ] Platform: add automated prewarm step at canary ramp to pre-populate common prefixes (Ruth Alvarez).
- [ ] Metrics: add canary/stable sample parity check to detect cache divergence earlier (Liam Chen).
- [ ] Release: revise pin-duration policy to allow instant pin on automated rollback but keep 5m manual hold for investigation (Aisha Khan).
- [ ] QA: generate synthetic long-context workloads to validate future canaries (QA team).

Loose notes / brainstorming (unstructured):
- Could try staggered prefix-affinity routing: route users with high prefix reuse to canary first to warm cache. Risk: introduces sampling bias.
- Think about a dynamic prewarm that inspects trending prefixes in last 24h and seeds them. Might be heavy on tokens but reduces cold penalties.
- Consider a short-lived dual-run mode: run requests on both stable and canary for a subset and compare both latency and top-k logits — helpful but doubles compute cost.

Open questions to resolve before next attempt:
- How to quantify acceptable cache warmup cost vs. production token spend? (calc needed)
- Should we add an explicit canary-only warmup window (e.g., 30m synthetic prewarm) before routing live traffic?
- Can we get telemetries earlier than 1m granularity for p99 to reduce reaction lag?

Notes-to-self (reminders):
- Keep snapshots of logs + traces for 48h beyond rollback.
- Create ticket ENG-1290 to track kernel-fallback work and link to this postmortem.
- Share brief summary with PM and CS so they can prep customer comms if asked.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to formal postmortem + checklist once follow-ups are assigned and first fixes land.
